lit: able to speak and good at talking

use.how: Describes a person, as a predicate or before 的: 她很能说会道。 Usually admiring, sometimes hinting the talk outruns the substance.

near.diff: 花言巧语 is the deceptive talk itself and always criticises; 能说会道 describes a person's skill with words and is often praise.
口若悬河 is more literary and pictures a long, unstoppable flow of speech; 能说会道 is everyday and stresses persuasiveness.

cue: Your cousin always has the right words ready and can talk a shop owner into a discount. How do you describe her?

ctx.s: 她从小就{能说会道}，大人都说她长大能当律师。
ctx.en: She has had a way with words since she was little; the adults all say she could become a lawyer.

ctx.s: 我们需要一个{能说会道}的人去跟客户谈。
ctx.en: We need someone who can really talk to go and negotiate with the client.

ctx.s: 别看他平时不爱说话，到了谈判桌上却特别{能说会道}。
ctx.en: He may not say much normally, but at the negotiating table he is a real talker.

ctx.s: 你这么{能说会道}，怎么不去做销售？
ctx.en: You're so persuasive, why don't you go into sales?

ctx.s: 那个推销员{能说会道}，没几分钟就让我妈买了一台净水器。
ctx.en: The salesman was such a smooth talker that within minutes he had my mum buying a water purifier.

ctx.s: 光{能说会道}没用，客户最后看的还是产品质量。
ctx.en: Being a good talker isn't enough; in the end the customer looks at the quality of the product.

bad.s: 这位科学家的论文写得{能说会道}。
bad.en: (meant: the scientist's paper is well written)
bad.why: It describes a person's skill in speaking, not the quality of a piece of writing.

bad.s: 他{能说会道}了三种外语。
bad.en: (meant: he can speak three foreign languages)
bad.why: It is not about knowing languages and cannot take an object; it describes being persuasive and fluent with words.

mean: bold and confident, sure one is in the right
lit: the reasoning is straight, so the spirit is strong

use.how: Mostly an adverbial with 地 before a verb of speaking or demanding: 理直气壮地说. Often used ironically of someone who is in fact in the wrong.

near.diff: 心安理得 is an inner feeling of being at peace with what one did; 理直气壮 is the bold, outward way one speaks or acts in a dispute.

cue: You were overcharged and have the receipt to prove it. How should you go back to the shop and complain?

ctx.s: 这件事你没做错，可以{理直气壮}地跟他说。
ctx.en: You did nothing wrong here, so you can tell him so with your head held high.

ctx.s: 既然发票齐全，财务再拖，你就{理直气壮}地去问他们要。
ctx.en: Since all your receipts are in order, if the accounts office keeps stalling, go and demand the money from them with your head held high.

ctx.s: 店员说不能退货，她拿出购物小票，{理直气壮}地要求店长出来解释。
ctx.en: When the assistant refused a refund, she produced her receipt and firmly demanded that the manager come and explain.

ctx.s: 孩子被冤枉了，回答老师的时候声音不大，却很{理直气壮}。
ctx.en: The child had been wrongly accused; answering the teacher, he spoke quietly but with complete conviction.

ctx.s: 他迟到了一个小时，还{理直气壮}地怪我没提醒他。
ctx.en: He was an hour late and still had the nerve to blame me for not reminding him.

ctx.s: 钱是你借的，你凭什么说得这么{理直气壮}？
ctx.en: You're the one who borrowed the money; what gives you the right to sound so sure of yourself?

bad.s: 他在比赛中{理直气壮}，跑得特别快。
bad.en: (meant: he was full of energy in the race and ran fast)
bad.why: It is about the confidence of being in the right in a dispute, not physical energy or strength.

bad.s: 她第一次上台演讲，非常{理直气壮}，一点也不紧张。
bad.en: (meant: she was confident and relaxed in her first speech)
bad.why: It needs a question of right and wrong; calm confidence on stage is simply being self-assured, not this.

story.text: Confucius warned in the Analects that clever words and an ingratiating face are seldom found with true goodness. Explaining that line to his students, the Song-dynasty scholar Zhu Xi said that such clever words are what people of his own day called by this phrase, an early record of the phrase often cited by dictionaries.

use.how: Used as a noun, often as the object of 听, 信, 用 or 被…骗: 别信他的花言巧语。 Always implies the words are meant to deceive.

near.diff: 甜言蜜语 is sweet, flattering talk, often between lovers and not always dishonest; 花言巧语 stresses that the fine words are a trick.
能说会道 describes a person who speaks well and can be praise; 花言巧语 is the deceitful talk itself and is always negative.

cue: A stranger on the phone promises your grandmother huge returns if she transfers her savings today. What is she hearing?

ctx.s: 别信他的{花言巧语}，他上次也是这么说的。
ctx.en: Don't believe his fine talk; he said exactly the same thing last time.

ctx.s: 骗子用一番{花言巧语}，骗走了老人一辈子的积蓄。
ctx.en: With a stream of smooth lies, the con man cheated the old man out of his life savings.

ctx.s: 她早就看穿了那个推销员的{花言巧语}。
ctx.en: She saw through the salesman's slick patter long ago.

ctx.s: 你以为编几句{花言巧语}就能骗我把钱借给你吗？
ctx.en: Do you think a few made-up smooth words will trick me into lending you money?

ctx.s: 网上那些稳赚不赔的投资广告，全靠{花言巧语}吸引人。
ctx.en: Those online ads for no-risk investments draw people in with nothing but clever talk.

ctx.s: 法官没有被他的{花言巧语}打动，还是判他赔偿全部损失。
ctx.en: The judge was not swayed by his glib words and still ordered him to pay for all the losses.

bad.s: 老师的讲解{花言巧语}，我们都听懂了。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher's explanation was vivid and we all understood)
bad.why: It is always a criticism of deceptive talk, never praise for a lively or clear explanation.

bad.s: 他写给我的生日祝福全是{花言巧语}，我感动得哭了。
bad.en: (meant: his birthday message was full of beautiful words and moved me to tears)
bad.why: Using it says the words are insincere tricks, which contradicts being genuinely moved.

lit: swallowing and spitting out, again and again: words that keep getting stuck

use.how: Describes how someone speaks, as an adverbial or predicate: 吞吞吐吐地说, 说话吞吞吐吐. Implies they are reluctant or afraid to say something.

near.diff: 支支吾吾 is mumbling to dodge a question; 吞吞吐吐 is more general hesitation over something hard to say.
拐弯抹角 is talking fluently but indirectly; 吞吞吐吐 is halting, broken speech.

cue: Your friend keeps starting a sentence, stopping and looking away, clearly afraid to tell you something. How is she talking?

ctx.s: 你别{吞吞吐吐}的，一句话断了好几次，到底想说什么？
ctx.en: Stop hemming and hawing; you have broken off that sentence several times. What are you trying to say?

ctx.s: 问他昨晚去哪儿了，他{吞吞吐吐}地说不清楚。
ctx.en: When asked where he went last night, he hesitated and couldn't give a straight answer.

ctx.s: 她{吞吞吐吐}了半天，才说出想借钱的事。
ctx.en: She hesitated for ages before finally saying she wanted to borrow money.

ctx.s: 你今天说话怎么{吞吞吐吐}的，是不是出什么事了？
ctx.en: Why are you so hesitant when you talk today? Has something happened?

ctx.s: 面试官一问到离职原因，他就变得{吞吞吐吐}起来。
ctx.en: As soon as the interviewer asked why he left his last job, he started to falter.

ctx.s: 医生说话有点{吞吞吐吐}，我心里一下子紧张了。
ctx.en: The doctor seemed reluctant to get the words out, and I suddenly felt nervous.

bad.s: 这台旧打印机{吞吞吐吐}，一张纸要印好久。
bad.en: (meant: the old printer is slow)
bad.why: It describes a person's hesitant speech, not a slow machine.

bad.s: 他吃饭{吞吞吐吐}，一碗面吃了半小时。
bad.en: (meant: he eats slowly)
bad.why: Despite the literal image of swallowing, it is only used about speaking, never about eating.

lit: discussion coming thick and fast from all sides

use.how: A predicate with a plural subject (大家, 人们, 网友们) reacting to some event: 消息传开后，大家议论纷纷。 Also 引得…议论纷纷.

near.diff: 七嘴八舌 is a group all talking at once in one noisy moment; 议论纷纷 is many people commenting on an event, often with differing views.
满城风雨 is a scandal that the whole town knows about; 议论纷纷 is simply widespread discussion and need not be scandalous.

cue: The company suddenly announces a new boss, and for days the staff talk about little else in the corridors and group chats. How do you describe them?

ctx.s: 公司突然换了总经理，员工们{议论纷纷}。
ctx.en: The company suddenly changed its general manager, and the staff were all talking about it.

ctx.s: 这条新闻一发出来，网友们{议论纷纷}。
ctx.en: As soon as the news came out, people online were all discussing it.

ctx.s: 比赛结果公布后，观众{议论纷纷}，觉得裁判不公平。
ctx.en: After the result was announced, the audience was abuzz, many feeling the referee had been unfair.

ctx.s: 这几天小区里{议论纷纷}的，到底发生了什么事？
ctx.en: The whole estate has been abuzz for days; what on earth has happened?

ctx.s: 关于学校要不要取消午休，家长们{议论纷纷}，意见很不一致。
ctx.en: Parents are debating whether the school should drop the midday rest, and opinions are sharply divided.

ctx.s: 他俩突然一起出现在婚礼上，引得亲戚们{议论纷纷}。
ctx.en: The two of them suddenly turning up at the wedding together set the relatives talking.

bad.s: 我一个人在房间里{议论纷纷}。
bad.en: (meant: I was alone in my room thinking it over)
bad.why: It needs many people talking among themselves; one person alone cannot be said to do this.

bad.s: 老师上课讲得{议论纷纷}，很有意思。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher's lecture was lively)
bad.why: It describes many people discussing an event, not the style of one speaker.

lit: a mouth gone mute, without a word

use.how: A predicate or result complement, usually after being challenged or refuted: 被问得哑口无言, 说得他哑口无言. About having no reply, not about awe.

near.diff: 张口结舌 is being tongue-tied from shock or nerves; 哑口无言 is having no answer to an argument or question.

cue: In an argument, your brother is shown the bank statement proving he spent the money, and he has nothing left to say. How is he?

ctx.s: 她一句话就把他问得{哑口无言}。
ctx.en: With one question she left him without an answer.

ctx.s: 证据摆在面前，他{哑口无言}。
ctx.en: With the evidence laid out in front of him, he had nothing to say.

ctx.s: 孩子反问：“你自己不也天天玩手机吗？”爸爸一下子{哑口无言}。
ctx.en: The child shot back, "Don't you play on your phone every day too?" and Dad was suddenly stuck for a reply.

ctx.s: 你刚才不是很能说吗，现在怎么{哑口无言}了？
ctx.en: Weren't you full of arguments a minute ago? Why have you got nothing to say now?

ctx.s: 辩论赛上，对方一个问题就让我们队{哑口无言}。
ctx.en: In the debate, a single question from the other side left our team with no answer.

ctx.s: 面对记者的追问，那位发言人{哑口无言}，场面十分尴尬。
ctx.en: Pressed by reporters, the spokesperson could find no reply, and the moment was very awkward.

bad.s: 看到这么美的风景，我{哑口无言}。
bad.en: (meant: the scenery was so beautiful it left me speechless)
bad.why: It means having no reply to a challenge, not being lost for words with awe at something beautiful.

bad.s: 图书馆里很安静，大家都{哑口无言}地看书。
bad.en: (meant: everyone read quietly in the library)
bad.why: It is not about being quiet; it means being unable to answer after being challenged.

mean: to embellish a story in the retelling
lit: to add oil and add vinegar, as when seasoning a dish

use.how: A predicate or adverbial about retelling an event with invented details: 添油加醋地说, 经过别人添油加醋. The core of the story is real.

near.diff: 无中生有 is making up something that never happened; 添油加醋 starts from a real event and adds made-up details.
夸大其词 is overstating size or degree; 添油加醋 is adding colourful extra details when passing a story on.

cue: Two neighbours had a short quarrel, but by the time the story has gone round the building it includes shouting, threats and a broken door. What has happened to the story?

ctx.s: 你照实说就行，别{添油加醋}。
ctx.en: Just tell it the way it happened; don't dress it up.

ctx.s: 这件事被他{添油加醋}地一说，听起来特别吓人。
ctx.en: The way he embellished it, the whole thing sounded terrifying.

ctx.s: 本来只是吵了两句，经过几个人{添油加醋}，就传成了打架。
ctx.en: It was only a brief argument, but after a few people embroidered it, the story became a fight.

ctx.s: 这些细节是真的，还是你{添油加醋}编出来的？
ctx.en: Are these details true, or did you make them up to spice the story up?

ctx.s: 有些自媒体为了流量，把普通的小事{添油加醋}，写成惊人的新闻。
ctx.en: Some online accounts embellish ordinary little incidents into shocking news just to get clicks.

ctx.s: 奶奶讲年轻时的故事，每次都要{添油加醋}一番，越讲越精彩。
ctx.en: Every time Grandma tells stories from her youth she adds a bit more, and they get better with each telling.

bad.s: 妈妈做菜时喜欢{添油加醋}，味道很好。
bad.en: (meant: Mum likes to add seasoning when she cooks)
bad.why: It is used only figuratively, about stories, never about actually seasoning food.

bad.s: 他把报告的数据{添油加醋}，修改得更准确了。
bad.en: (meant: he refined the data in the report to make it more accurate)
bad.why: It means distorting by adding false details, the opposite of making something more accurate.

mean: vying with one another to be first
lit: striving to be first and afraid of being last

use.how: An adverbial, usually with 地, describing a group rushing to do something: 孩子们争先恐后地举手。 Needs several people (or animals).

near.diff: 一拥而上 is a crowd surging forward all at once; 争先恐后 stresses each one trying to get ahead of the others.

cue: The teacher asks who wants to try the problem on the board, and every hand in the class shoots up, each child trying to be picked first. How do they raise their hands?

ctx.s: 下课铃一响，孩子们{争先恐后}地跑出教室。
ctx.en: The moment the bell rang, the children raced each other out of the classroom.

ctx.s: 老师一提问，同学们{争先恐后}地举手。
ctx.en: As soon as the teacher asked a question, the students all scrambled to put their hands up.

ctx.s: 商场打折第一天，顾客们{争先恐后}地往里挤。
ctx.en: On the first day of the sale, shoppers jostled one another to get inside.

ctx.s: 这款手机有什么特别的，大家为什么{争先恐后}地抢购？
ctx.en: What's so special about this phone that everyone is falling over themselves to buy it?

ctx.s: 地震发生后，志愿者们{争先恐后}地报名去灾区帮忙。
ctx.en: After the earthquake, volunteers rushed to sign up to help in the disaster area.

ctx.s: 小鸡一看到米粒，就{争先恐后}地围了过来。
ctx.en: As soon as the chicks saw the grains of rice, they crowded round, each trying to get there first.

bad.s: 我一个人{争先恐后}地赶到了车站。
bad.en: (meant: I hurried to the station)
bad.why: It describes several people competing to be first; one person alone cannot do it.

bad.s: 这次考试他{争先恐后}，得了第一名。
bad.en: (meant: he worked hard and came first in the exam)
bad.why: It pictures a group scrambling at one moment, not one person's effort or achievement.

lit: to pay back a tooth with a tooth

story.text: The phrase comes from the Chinese translation of the law of retaliation in the Hebrew Bible: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, rendered in Chinese as 'repay an eye with an eye, repay a tooth with a tooth'. In everyday Chinese the second half is now used on its own for hitting back in the same way one was hit.

use.how: A predicate or adverbial for retaliating in kind: 对他以牙还牙, 以牙还牙地骂回去. Only for paying back harm, never kindness.

near.diff: 针锋相对 is sharp opposition point against point, often in argument; 以牙还牙 is paying someone back with the same harm they did.

cue: A rival shop slashes its prices to steal your customers, so you immediately cut yours by the same amount. What are you doing?

ctx.s: 他骂我，我也不能{以牙还牙}地骂回去。
ctx.en: He swore at me, but I can't just swear back at him.

ctx.s: 弟弟抢了哥哥的玩具，哥哥{以牙还牙}，把弟弟的饼干也拿走了。
ctx.en: The younger brother grabbed his brother's toy, so the older one paid him back by taking his biscuits.

ctx.s: 对手在比赛中故意犯规，我们也不应该{以牙还牙}。
ctx.en: Even if the other team fouls on purpose, we shouldn't retaliate in kind.

ctx.s: 她在网上被人写文章嘲笑，干脆{以牙还牙}，也写了一篇文章讽刺对方。
ctx.en: Mocked in an online article, she simply hit back the same way and wrote a piece ridiculing them.

ctx.s: 那家公司降价抢客户，我们只好{以牙还牙}，也推出了优惠。
ctx.en: That company cut prices to steal customers, so we answered in kind with discounts of our own.

ctx.s: 别人怎么对你，你就怎么对别人，这样{以牙还牙}真的能解决问题吗？
ctx.en: Treating people exactly the way they treat you: can tit-for-tat really solve anything?

bad.s: 朋友帮我搬家，我请他吃饭，算是{以牙还牙}。
bad.en: (meant: my friend helped me move, so I repaid him with dinner)
bad.why: It is only for paying back harm or hostility; repaying a kindness needs a different expression.

bad.s: 他对我很{以牙还牙}。
bad.en: (meant: he treats me harshly)
bad.why: It names an act of retaliation and cannot be used as an adjective after a degree word like 'very'.

lit: to save on eating and be sparing in using

use.how: A predicate or adverbial about a person or family cutting their own living costs, often to save for something or someone: 父母省吃俭用供我上学。 Usually said with respect.

near.diff: 精打细算 is careful planning and calculation of spending; 省吃俭用 is denying oneself everyday comforts to save.
节衣缩食 is more written and suggests harsher deprivation of food and clothing; 省吃俭用 is the everyday phrase.

cue: For years your parents ate the cheapest food and never bought new clothes so they could pay your university fees. What did they do?

ctx.s: 父母{省吃俭用}，供我读完了大学。
ctx.en: My parents scrimped and saved to put me through university.

ctx.s: 她{省吃俭用}了好几年，终于买了一台钢琴。
ctx.en: She went without for several years and finally bought a piano.

ctx.s: 刚工作那几年，我{省吃俭用}，午饭常常只吃一个馒头。
ctx.en: In my first years at work I scrimped so hard that lunch was often just one steamed bun.

ctx.s: 你工资不低，为什么连一件新衣服都舍不得买，这么{省吃俭用}？
ctx.en: You earn a decent salary; why won't you even buy yourself a new piece of clothing? Why skimp like this?

ctx.s: 这笔钱是妈妈{省吃俭用}攒下来的，你可不能乱花。
ctx.en: Mum saved this money by going without, so don't you dare waste it.

ctx.s: 爷爷奶奶一辈子{省吃俭用}，自己舍不得花钱，却总给孙子买东西。
ctx.en: Grandma and Grandpa lived frugally all their lives, begrudging themselves every penny but always buying things for their grandchildren.

bad.s: 公司为了{省吃俭用}，裁掉了一半员工。
bad.en: (meant: the company laid off half its staff to cut costs)
bad.why: It is about a person or family cutting their own living expenses, not a company cutting costs or staff.

bad.s: 这台空调很{省吃俭用}，一个月用不了多少电。
bad.en: (meant: this air conditioner is energy-efficient)
bad.why: It describes people cutting their own food and living costs, never a machine that uses little power; for that, say it saves electricity.
